_rules: Each key is a first name a suspect could have: one word of at most 9 letters, A to Z with or without accents, starting with a capital and not all capitals.
Each riddle is a noun phrase that completes 'Police have arrested ___' and opens '___ is next to the killer'.
A riddle must point to exactly one first name, and must not contain that name.
Keep it REALLY easy: the answer should be in the first one or two search results for the riddle.
Use the name everyone uses (Ringo, not Richard). No full stop at the end.
The same riddle must never appear under two names.
A riddle is a plain line, or an object that holds it as riddle along with any of places, victim, level, keep_off and who. A plain line is the same as an object holding only its riddle.

places: a list of codes for where the riddle is common knowledge. The places are US, GB-ENG (England), GB-SCT (Scotland), GB-WLS (Wales) and GB-NIR (Northern Ireland). The groups are GB (the United Kingdom: all four nations) and GB-GBN (Great Britain: England, Scotland and Wales). Write GB, not UK. A riddle counts for a group only if it counts in every place of that group. Leave places out and the riddle counts everywhere.
victim: true or false, whether the riddle may name the victim. Left out, it is true.
level: easy, medium or hard. Left out, it is easy.

keep_off: a list of first names that must not be on a board where the riddle is used. A name from this table that the riddle prints, starting with a capital, is kept off by itself; list only the names the table lacks.
who: a note for people on who the riddle means.
